concerns.text: FR-006 introduces Benjamini‑Hochberg correction for multiple hypothesis tests, but the original idea only specified a single t‑test comparison. This adds a new methodological layer not requested and constitutes scope over‑reach.

FR-007 requires a stratified random sample of detected vulnerabilities for manual audit to estimate precision/recall. The idea did not call for any ground‑truth audit or tool accuracy assessment, so this is an unrequested feature that expands the scope beyond the core research question.

FR-008 mandates calculation of false‑positive rates per tool and CWE and adjustment of vulnerability counts accordingly. The original idea never mentioned correcting counts for tool error rates, making this a new analysis dimension not required for comparing vulnerability density.

SC-006 sets precision and recall thresholds (≥ 80 %) for the static analysis tools. These performance metrics were not part of the initial research question and therefore represent unnecessary additional deliverables.

SC-007 requires reporting a disparity in false‑positive rates between LLM‑generated and human code, with a deferred trigger for follow‑up. This metric was not defined in the idea and adds a new investigative focus.
SC-003 imposes a hard execution‑time limit (≤ 6 hours) on the analysis. The idea did not specify any runtime constraints; this operational bound is extraneous to the scientific scope.
SC-004 caps peak memory usage at 7 GB RAM. Like SC-003, this is an engineering constraint not mentioned in the original idea and thus extends the scope beyond what was requested.

SC-005 demands that at least 95 % of files be successfully analyzed. The idea did not set a success threshold for file‑level coverage, making this an additional requirement not required to answer the research question.
